diagnosis: The best code has about 490 pairs tied at the maximum cosine within $10^{-12}$, averaging roughly six contacts per point with counts from 3 to 9 and zero rattlers. Since points on $S^3$ have $3\cdot163-6=483$ degrees of freedom after global rotations, this contact graph is slightly over-isostatic and rigidly jammed: it has essentially no nontrivial floppy motion along which contacts can reorganise. The next pairs sit only about $10^{-5}$ below the maximum, so local softmax, L-BFGS, and trust-region LP steps are blocked by the active contacts while remaining too close to the second tier to make finite single-point jumps, explaining why 33 variants collapse to the identical score $0.8564120867749$. The missing structural property is therefore not better local optimality but an unlocked degree of freedom—a rattler/floppy subcluster, deliberately broken contact set, or symmetry-enforced collective mode—that permits a different contact topology.
